name: Pampadromaeus
sum: Pampadromaeus is a basal sauropodomorph from the Late Triassic (Carnian) Santa Maria Formation of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, with a mosaic of basal and derived traits.
wsnote: No body-size figure was read in the sources consulted.
holotype: ULBRA-PVT016, a disarticulated but well preserved partial skeleton of one individual (Alemoa Member, "Janner" locality).
material: Known from the holotype only, with most skull bones and lower jaws, dorsal, sacral and tail vertebrae, shoulder girdle and forelimb elements, an ilium and hindlimb elements.
biology: Some traits are shared with theropods, such as a downturned premaxilla and unserrated front teeth; its skull suggests that the pneumatisation of archosaur groups evolved independently at least three times.
author: Cabreira et al. 2011

sources.text: S. F. Cabreira, C. L. Schultz, and J. S. Bittencourt, M. B. Soares, D. C. Fortier, L. R. Silva, M. C. Langer. 2011. New stem-sauropodomorph (Dinosauria, Saurischia) from the Triassic of Brazil. Naturwissenschaften 98(12):1035-1040
